text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Syrian President Assad received Prime Minister Hariri in Damascus for four hours.

-Council of Maronite Bishops said: The delay in handing over official documents on parliamentary elections to the constitutional court which is studying appeals lodged by defeated candidates "weakened confidence in public institutions".
-Israeli forces detain a surgeon in the occupied zone and shell areas in the south.
-Lebanon's biggest company Solidere starts marketing Global Depository Receipts worth $125 million.
-Hariri tries to bring more of his supporters into the new cabinet under formation.

-The European Union will grant Lebanon $650 million next month in Washington at the "consultative group" meeting. The group was formed under an April 26 ceasefire understanding that brought to an end 17 days of Israeli bombardment of Lebanon.
-Christian Maronite Patriarch Sfeir heads to the Vatican today.
-Gas stations will go on one-day strike tomorrow.
